definitions.explanation: The act of telling a story or relating events orally. Also refers to the narrative style or the narrator's voice in a performance or literary work.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}の{語|かた}りに{引|ひ}き{込|こ}まれた。
examples.english: I was drawn into her narration.

examples.japanese: この{映画|えいが}は{語|かた}りが{美|うつく}しい。
{祖母|そぼ}の{戦争|せんそう}{体験|たいけん}の{語|かた}りは、いつも{胸|むね}に{迫|せま}るものがあった。
examples.english: My grandmother's narration of her wartime experiences was always deeply moving.

notes:
{語|かた}り is the noun form of {語|かた}る (to narrate, to tell). It refers both to the act of narration and to the narrative itself.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {語|かた}り{部|べ} (storyteller; keeper of oral tradition)
- {語|かた}り{口|くち} (way of speaking, narrative style)
- {語|かた}り{手|て} (narrator, storyteller)
- {物語|ものがたり}の{語|かた}り (narration of a tale)

In traditional Japanese performing arts, {語|かた}り refers to the narrative component of forms like {能|のう} and {浄瑠璃|じょうるり}, where a performer recites the story while others act or manipulate puppets.
